evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh and the scoring script /opt/score_golden.py, and did initial inspection of golden.jsonl structure — solid orientation on the contract mechanics.
Enumerated the ~12 LSP methods present, computed a per-method frequency breakdown, and counted the 1007 java files / 68k test entries — enumeration of what is tested.
Inferred a real contract detail: didOpen sends empty text so the server must read files from disk — evidence of understanding beyond surface skimming.

Repeatedly stated intent to 'understand exact response formats' and sampled entries, but never derived per-method format invariants (position indexing, URI scheme, range boundaries, capabilities handshake).

Pivoted to a golden-lookup approach keyed by (file, method, line, char), which deliberately removed any need to reverse-engineer per-method response shapes — so the deep format dissection anchored at level 8 never occurred.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared the level-5 bar: it read run_tests and the scorer, enumerated the tested methods and files, and inferred basic contract mechanics (disk-reading on didOpen). However it never reached level 8: it repeatedly announced but never actually built an explicit per-method format spec (indexing, URI scheme, range boundaries, capabilities), because its lookup pivot made detailed format understanding unnecessary. This places observed behavior squarely at 5 — enumeration and basic schema awareness without systematic per-method reverse-engineering.
